speaker: Mr Leon Perera
text: asked the Minister for Law (a) what is the average timespan of a manually-handled court case as compared to one managed under the Integrated Case Management System (ICMS); (b) what is the number of State Courts cases that have been adjourned over the ICMS system failure on 7 February 2023; and (c) what is the typical frequency and duration of ICMS maintenance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The State Courts decide on matters relating to their case management systems, such as procurement and maintenance.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The following is based on information received from the State Courts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: The ICMS is used to manage all criminal cases in the State Courts.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Judges and litigants may use ICMS to access case records, schedule hearings, upload documents, file applications and generate Court orders.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Scheduled maintenance is carried out after Court operating hours to minimise disruptions to users.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: After the disruption to ICMS happened, the State Courts activated their business continuity plans to ensure that Court hearings could proceed despite the disruption.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: This included printing hard copy documents, where appropriate, for parties to refer to and Judges recording their notes on Microsoft Word.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: As a result, the vast majority of criminal cases were not affected.

speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Law (Ms Rahayu Mahzam) (for the Minister for Law)
text: Minimal disruption was caused to these adjourned cases.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: Just two supplementary questions and I understand, of course, that you will have to relay this information from the State Courts.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: The first question is: is there a plan to overhaul the system?

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: It seems to me that weekly maintenance that can take between four and 10 hours is quite burdensome and there is also feedback from some lawyers that the system is a bit clunky and slow, and sometimes, glitchy – that was reported in the media article.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: So, I am wondering if there is going to be a more thorough overhaul coming up in the future.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: And my second question is, I understand that the system for requesting criminal case management conferences is, right now, not integrated with ICMS.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: You would have to go to a separate page on the Attorney-General's Chambers (AGC) website.

speaker: Mr Leon Perera (Aljunied)
text: So, is there a plan to integrate that functionality into ICMS?

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I want to clarify on the point of the timing for the maintenance.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: In a way, it is a small number.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: The second point I want to mention is the fact that we note some of the feedback given by the lawyers.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: I know that it was largely coming out from the article, so I am not sure if it is necessarily representative.

speaker: Ms Rahayu Mahzam
text: But that is something we can look into and I take the feedback back.
